description: Plan v7 section 8.3 fixture family 'owed-validator'. Inputs only; the oracle emits expected.

cases.notes: THE CONTROL. A programmatic catalog carrying a plain node, a well-formed language-form placeholder and a valid whole-message alternative CONSTRUCTS, and the probe answers 'Hello'. Every refusal in this family differs from this fixture in exactly one member, so without this row a port that refused ALL programmatic catalogs would pass the whole family.

LocalizedStringValidator:212, and DefaultStrings:297 is the site that reaches it. The discriminator is the refusal IDENTITY: a port that accepts an empty translations map, or refuses it with a different exception or message, differs here and nowhere else. Read against owed-validator.control.programmatic-catalog-constructs, whose 'Items' node carries the same placeholder with a NON-empty map.
LocalizedStringValidator:230, plus invalid():327's cause-less arm. Read against the control's 'Items' node, which differs only in that both of its forms come from one axis.

LocalizedStringValidator:233. ONE non-cardinal form, not two: two would be refused by :230 a line earlier and this row would close a branch it never entered -- the zh-123 shape, where an input rejected by an earlier guard 'confirms' a check it never reached.

LocalizedStringValidator:312's !isValidLocalizedStringIdentifier disjunct. Its sibling disjunct (identifier == null) is unreachable -- every caller passes a value already established non-null, re-probed on the pinned Corretto 21 against the one caller that could plausibly present one (the placeholderDefinitions map key, which LocalizedString.Builder refuses first). CORRECTED 2026-09-09: this note used to end 'which is why the line stays required on this arm alone', and that was already false when it shipped -- the same slice moved LocalizedStringValidator#validateIdentifier:312 from required to EXCLUDED, on the strength of exactly this unreachability plus the coverage this case buys. The disposition is the measured record; a case note asserting a branch's own status is how two texts end up making one false claim, which is the shape M3b already paid for once.

LocalizedStringValidator:314. Read against owed-validator.refusal.invalid-identifier: both names reach validateIdentifier, and only the reserved one carries the ': language-form constants are reserved' clause, so a port with one rejection where Java has two differs on exactly one of these two rows.

LocalizedStringValidator's validateTemplate and invalid():327's CAUSED arm -- the only refusal in this family that retains a cause, which is the whole reason it is here: every other row exercises invalid()'s cause-less spelling and none of them distinguishes the two. Read against owed-validator.control.programmatic-catalog-constructs, whose 'Items' node carries a well-formed reference to the same kind of template.
